entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: List has been revised.
Learned counsel for the informant is not present.
2. Rejoinder affidavit filed today is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Pawan Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
4.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.121 of 2021 registered under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506 and 120B IPC at Police Station- Mahila Thana, District Saharanpur with a prayer to enlarge her on anticipatory bail.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that co-accused person Mohd. Tahir has already been granted anticipatory bail by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 10.8.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No.7101 of 2022.

Therefore, the Gulista vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67114731/
1
present applicant is also entitled for anticipatory bail on the ground of parity.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant undertakes that she will cooperate in the trial failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of the anticipatory bail.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant has also placed much reliance upon the judgement of Apex Court passed in Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs. The State of Bihar, 2022(6) SCC 599, whereby it has been categorically stated that the Courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs. The State of Bihar, 2022(6) SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.
Learned counsel has further stated that the applicant lives separately in the house opposite to the house of husband of the informant.
7. The prayer for anticipatory bail has been vehemently opposed by learned A.G.A.
However, the aforesaid factual aspect of the parity to the co-accused has not been disputed by her.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, pending trial and in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Nanha S/o Nabhan Kha vs. State of U.P., 1993 Crl.L.J. 938 and the judgement passed by the Apex Court in Paras Ram Vishnoi vs. The Director, Central Bureau of Investigation,
MANU/SCOR/22410/2021, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Nanha S/o Nabhan Kha vs. State of U.P., 1993 Crl.L.J. 938
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Paras Ram Vishnoi vs. The Director, Central Bureau of Investigation,
MANU/SCOR/22410/2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The anticipatory bail application is allowed on the ground of parity.
9. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
10. It is made clear that observations made hereinabove are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial.
Order Date :- 15.2.2024

Ravi Kant (Krishan Pahal, J.)
